correctness.rationale: The Wiener-growth recurrence is exact conditional on each earlier tree. Conditioning on a marked root attachment changes the initial conditional expectation by 3(j-1)-(j+1)H_(j-1), while every future step scales the difference by (m+2)/m. Bernoulli covariance gives the local formula. The ratio (j+1)H_(j-1)/(j-1) equals 3 at j=2,3 and strictly increases thereafter by a harmonic bound, so all later contributions are negative. Swapping finite sums yields the displayed global identity and the pi-squared limit. Exact exhaustive enumeration of 5913 trees through size 8 and 149 more finite identity checks independently corroborated the derived results; they are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected recursive-tree Wiener literature establishes expectation/limits and covariance with internal path length, not covariance with the root child count. A published local root-attachment covariance for total root path length is a different statistic and does not imply the Wiener covariance. Distinct other published results address leaf or Zagreb index interactions. The arrival-by-arrival exact Wiener law and strict threshold were not identified in the actual searches; this is qualified best-knowledge originality, subject to older unpublished or unstated corollaries.

value.rationale: The Wiener index is a canonical global distance statistic and root degree is a canonical local growth/centrality statistic. The complete marked-arrival profile isolates exactly two neutral early arrivals, proves strict negative influence for each later root attachment uniformly in final tree size, and gives a nontrivial quadratic covariance constant. This goes beyond routine recomputation of a marginal mean and exposes interaction of all-pairs distance with the growth history.
